title: Access transition: SAML assertion audit and dual-sync plan
creator: Aisha N. Park
description: We need a low-risk operational plan to migrate customer access state from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 while preserving SAML/SSO assertions and audit continuity. This ticket covers: (1) dual-sync (v1->v2 write mirroring) and shadow-backfill strategies, (2) enriched SAML assertion audit logging to the new audit pipeline, (3) admin-mode controls for staged cutover and emergency rollback, and (4) customer communications and opt-in for early waves. Goal: zero-permission-drift for customers after cutover and full audit lineage for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Dual-sync implementation merges writes to both v1 and v2 for create/update/delete ops with <2s additional median latency for auth flows
Backfill job completes for all historical permission records with reconciliation report showing <=0.01% mismatches and documented remediation plan
SAML assertion events are produced to the new audit topic with consistent schema and retained for required retention period
Canary group (5% customers) completes 72h smoke window with no auth regressions and <0.1% increase in latency errors
Administrative cutover tool allows operator to toggle read/write routing and performs automated verification post-switch
Customer-facing communication draft and admin runbook published and reviewed by Legal and Support
Security review completed and signed off by InfoSec with mitigation for key risks
notes: Decision: implement dual-sync (write to v1 and v2) rather than traffic-only proxy to minimize one-off code paths; this keeps current auth code stable
Trade-off: dual-sync increases write amplification; we will mitigate with batching and backpressure windows during heavy migrations
Implementation detail: use the event-streaming layer (kafka cluster cluster-a) to fan-out writes to v2 service asynchronously with at-least-once semantics
Reconciliation strategy: nightly reconciliation job computes canonical diff and emits prioritized remediation tasks; threshold for automatic remediate = <=100 user-permissions per org
SAML audit change: embed original SAML assertion id and in-reply-to fields into audit schema (v3) to preserve traceability for compliance audits
Admin controls: build an operator endpoint (/admin/rbac-cutover) gated by SSO and mfa, which provides dry-run validation, enable/disable switch, and safety timers
Rollback plan: switch reads back to v1 and run reconciliation until discrepancy rate is zero; keep write-dualation enabled for 48h after rollback before turning off
Metrics to monitor: mismatch_rate, auth_latency_p50/p95, error_rate_5m, audit_event_lag, reconciliation_backlog
Docs: Confluence design doc linked, runbook skeleton in progress, PR template created for each subtask
Stakeholders: Legal (policy), Compliance (audit retention), Support (customer comms), Platform (kafka ownership), Console (observability)
